Tom / team — detailed answers below (high level first, then specifics). Happy to expand on any item or jump on a call.

High-level summary:
- Supported BYOK modes: wrapped-key import (recommended for hosted), HSM-mediated import for Dedicated/Private deployments, and in-place customer-managed HSM integrations via KMIP where applicable.
- Envelope encryption: Redwood uses envelope encryption by default. Customer master keys (CMKs) are used to wrap per-tenant data keys (DEKs). Rotations are versioned; DEKs re-encrypt new objects on write and are migrated lazily for older objects.
- Attestations: For keys imported into Redwood-managed HSMs, we can provide attestation reports (signed statements from the HSM vendor) and audit trail of import operations. For Private deployments, customers can choose to keep keys exclusively in their HSM.

Specifics:
1) Accepted import formats and wrapping
- Hosted product: we accept wrapped key blobs only (RSA-OAEP or AES-KWP wrapping). We publish a per-import ephemeral public wrapping key (RSA 3072 or ECC P-384) for each import session. We do NOT accept plaintext raw key material through the public hosted API.
- Dedicated/Private: support both wrapped imports and raw key material delivered over secure channels during a controlled key-ceremony (physical or virtual) into the HSM.

2) HSM and attestation
- We operate HSMs that meet FIPS 140-2 Level 3 / FIPS 140-3 equivalent when using vetted vendors (CloudHSM / Azure Dedicated HSM / on-prem Thales/Entrust for Private).
- Attestation artifacts: signed attestation statement (vendor-specific format), import operation audit record (timestamped, operator id, import-session id), and an import-token binding record. Sample attestation (signed ASN.1 blob) can be provided on request.

3) Key rotation
- Default rotation cadence: 90 days for wrapping keys; customer can configure CMK rotation to any interval or trigger rotations manually via API.
- Rotation model: CMKs are versioned. New DEKs are wrapped with the new CMK version. For zero-downtime, Redwood keeps prior CMK versions available for decryption until all objects migrate or the customer retires older versions.

4) Tenant isolation and multi-tenancy
- Hosted: cryptographic isolation via per-tenant CMKs (logical separation) stored in HSM key slots with strict access controls; runtime processes use tenant-scoped key handles, not raw keys. Admin plane and data plane are separated — operators do not have direct access to raw customer key material.
- Dedicated/Private: physical isolation options (dedicated HSM pool and VPC-only access).

5) TLS & ciphers
- Supported: TLS 1.2 (secure ciphers only) and TLS 1.3. We prefer TLS 1.3 with AEAD ciphers (AES-GCM, CHACHA20-POLY1305). We enforce perfect forward secrecy (ECDHE).
- mTLS: supported for Redwood Private / Dedicated deployments; for hosted API mTLS is available for specific enterprise contracts.

6) Auditing and log export
- Key usage logs: retained by default for 13 months in the control plane (configurable up to 7 years under enterprise agreements).
- Exports: real-time streaming to customer SIEM via secure webhook or S3 export; periodic CSV bundles via secure share; audit records include operation type, key id, actor, timestamp, source IP, request id.

Attachments included: redwood-kms-diagram.png (high-level keyflow), a sample import attestation (redwood-sample-attestation.txt available upon NDA), and the integration guide PDF.

If you need the public wrapping key for testing, I can generate an ephemeral import session and share that public key — it takes ~1 business hour.

Tom — good questions, quick clarifications below and I've uploaded artifacts to the shared folder.

1) Wrapping algorithms and key sizes: 
- RSA-OAEP (SHA-256) with RSA 3072 or RSA 4096 supported.
- AES Key Wrap with Padding (AES-KWP): we support AES-256-KWP for wrapped key material in hosted scenarios.

2) Attestation artifact format and sample
- We provide an HSM attestation bundle that contains: (a) vendor-signed attestation statement (ASN.1 DER), (b) import-session id and timestamp, (c) key-id fingerprint, (d) operator-id (redacted when required), and (e) HSM firmware/serial info.
- Uploaded: redwood-sample-attestation.txt (redacted), and an HTML rendering of canonical attestation fields in the shared Drive (link in related_links). These are suitable for compliance ingestion; if you need vendor-specific schema (CloudHSM/Azure HSM/Thales), tell us which and we'll provide that variant.

3) Import-session key lifecycle
- Hosted: ephemeral per-import public wrapping keys are issued for each import session (short-lived, single use) — this reduces replay risk. We can support a predictable registration model for automation using a service-account flow (we issue a registration token that allows Stellar to request ephemeral wrapping keys programmatically).
- Dedicated/Private: customers can upload PKCS#12 or raw key material during a controlled ceremony (PKCS#12 accepted when delivered through the private channel or customer-managed HSM integration).

Timeline and next steps:
- I created a sample import session and placed the public wrapping key and a sample wrapped blob in the shared Drive folder.
- Expected turnaround to provide a per-session public key on request: ~1 hour during business hours.
- Attestation sample and canonical fields are in the same folder (redwood-sample-attestation.txt).

If Stellar would like, we can schedule a 30-minute runthrough of the import flow this afternoon.

Regards,
